_note: Waivers for tools/replay_bench.py. A stored program that goes pass->fail, or moves into
silent_wrong, under a new binary is a regression unless it is waived here. Each block is keyed
by the CHANGELOG version that declared the break, and an entry names one program exactly
(task_id + sha256 of its source). A waiver applies only to reports whose binary predates that
version. Add entries only after checking that the declared change explains the flip; the
evidence field says how each one was checked.

2026-07-26-1.reason: Text is 0-based (CHANGELOG 2026-07-26-1): s[0] is the first character, and copy(s, start, count) takes a 0-based start. Programs written against the 1-based Text of 2026-06/07 boards (copy(s, i + 1, n), copy(s, i, 1) over 1..m, s[i] over 1..m) now print the wrong answer or index past the end. The entry predicts exactly this: such code still compiles and silently does the wrong thing.

2026-10-08-1.reason: L1 (CHANGELOG 2026-10-08-1) declares two breaks that reject programs which used to run. D17: NAME-001 ignores case and covers more scopes -- a parameter or local that reuses a top-level const or global name (in any letter case), and a loop variable that reuses an outer variable's name, are errors. W8-14 / D45: expression-shaped text after `//` is DIV-002 (`x // 5` is a comment in Aether, not integer division). Each program below passed on 2026-10-06-1 while containing one of these and is now stopped by exactly that diagnostic.

2026-10-13-1.reason: A slice of a field compiles (CHANGELOG 2026-10-13-1). A stored program that used to stop at `[SCOPE-001] identifier '__aether_slice_0' not in scope` now runs; where its own logic is wrong, the wrong output becomes visible. That is the fix exposing a program that was never right, not a miscompile.

entries.evidence: extractMin shrinks the heap with `self.data = self.data[0..(length(self.data) - 2)] + [];`, a half-open range that drops two elements per call, so 5 of 10 values are printed. 2026-10-08-1 stopped at the SCOPE-001 on that line; 2026-10-13-1 prints `sorted = 3 4 7 8 19`.
2026-10-08-1: [SCOPE-001] identifier '__aether_slice_0' not in scope; 2026-10-13-1 and later: compiles and prints `6, 9, 3, 7, 1, 8, 4, 2` (the input order), its own sort being wrong.

2026-10-07-1.reason: Nested `continue` works (L0, CHANGELOG 2026-10-07-1). On 2026-10-06-1 these trap_life_continue programs stopped with ARR-003, an out-of-range index caused by the baseline's nested-continue defect driving a loop past its bound. With continue working they run to the end and print a wrong grid because of their own logic: three count neighbours with `loop d in -1..1` (a half-open range that never visits one side), one prints the count and board rows alternately, one computes a correct step for a grid it transcribed wrongly. L0, L1 and later builds print identical output for each, so the move into silent-wrong is the fix exposing programs that were never right.

entries.evidence: 2026-10-06-1: ARR-003 from the nested-continue defect; L0 and later: runs, prints a wrong grid (own range or print-order or transcription error), identical on every later build.
